hints.title: Composite Frequency and Lexical Ordering
hints.text: Words must be ranked primarily by descending frequency and secondarily by alphabetical order. How can word occurrence counting establish this composite order?

hints.title: Two-Tier Sorting Comparator Invariant
hints.text: A composite sorting comparator comparing counts first in descending order, then string tie-breaking in lexicographical order, determines the ordering.

hints.title: Frequency Map Custom Sort Procedure
hints.text: Tally word frequencies across the input list. Sort unique words using a custom comparator that prioritizes higher frequency, breaking ties with alphabetical string comparison. Take the initial k elements.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting every word naively without grouping frequencies takes redundant comparison time and does not aggregate duplicates.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting frequencies takes O(N) time and sorting unique words takes O(U log U) where U <= N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle two-tier comparison: higher frequency comes first, but smaller lexicographical order comes first on ties.
